title: The Cost of Living
headline_read: Inflation has cooled but isn't beaten — still above target.

indicators.title: Inflation · CPI (year-over-year)
indicators.context: The Consumer Price Index — the headline measure of how fast the prices households actually pay are rising versus a year ago.
indicators.read: Running at 3.3% a year — still above the Fed's 2% goal.

indicators.title: Core CPI (year-over-year)
indicators.context: CPI excluding volatile food and energy. Because it strips out the noisiest prices, it's a better read on the economy's underlying inflation trend.
indicators.read: Running at 2.5% a year — close to the Fed's 2% goal.

indicators.title: PCE Inflation (year-over-year)
indicators.context: The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve watches most closely when setting interest rates.
indicators.read: Running at 3.7% a year — still above the Fed's 2% goal.

indicators.title: Core PCE Inflation (year-over-year)
indicators.context: PCE excluding food and energy — the measure the Fed's 2% target is actually stated in. When policymakers say “inflation,” this is the number they mean.
indicators.read: Running at 3.3% a year — still above the Fed's 2% goal.

indicators.title: Real Wage Growth (year-over-year)
indicators.context: The typical worker's weekly paycheck adjusted for inflation (real median earnings). When it rises, pay is outpacing prices; when it falls, the opposite.
indicators.read: Up 0.5% from a year ago — paychecks are outpacing inflation.
